ai.description: *Hydrophis spiralis* reaches 2.7m. It features a bright yellow body with narrow black rings and a small head. It is distinguished by 29–33 scale rows around the neck and 37–46 around the body.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Hydrophis spiralis* is uniquely identified by its high mid-body scale count (33–38 rows) and a distinct pattern of narrow black rings that widen into rhomboids dorsally.
ai.habitat: *Hydrophis spiralis* inhabits the tropical coastal waters of the Indian subcontinent, typically frequenting shallow, muddy-bottomed marine environments and coral reefs.
ai.behavior: Hydrophis spiralis is a highly active, diurnal predator that primarily hunts eels and other elongated fish by patrolling coral reefs and sandy seafloor habitats.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hydrophis spiralis* is ovoviviparous, typically producing litters of 6–16 young. Breeding occurs throughout the year, with peak activity observed from May to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Hydrophis spiralis* inhabits coastal waters across the Indian subcontinent, ranging from the Arabian Sea to the Bay of Bengal, primarily within shallow marine environments.
